newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's new privatisation head sees selloff push.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's new privatisation head sees selloff push.

text.p: The new head of Ukraine's state privatisation agency said on Thursday that Ukraine would fully privatise all medium- and large-scale enterprises this year.

"Eight thousand big and medium enterprises will at last be sold," Volodymyr Lanovy, acting chief of the State Property Fund (FDM), told reporters in his first public statement since being named to the position earlier this month.
Lanovy, whose position is expected to be confirmed by parliament soon, replaced Yuri Yekhanurov, who was appointed economy minister last month.
Ukraine completed last month privatisation of 5,000 out of 8,000 medium and large government holdings.
The 1997 plan calls for increasing share prices of newly-privatised enterprises on local exchanges, and eventual development of a stock index, Lanovy said.
"We could raise price levels of primary issues to market values," he said.
Trading on the Ukrainian Stock Exchange's weekly sessions is often thin. Ukraine also has two other exchanges and a Kiev-based over-the-counter system.
Lanovy added that companies would be ready to issue shares internationally one year after Ukraine issues a foreign bond, expected to happen sometime this year.
